narrative.overview: The site is one circuit board with the power on. The page ground is matte soldermask, and under the mask you can see the board's copper wherever the board is empty: buses of traces that turn in 45-degree steps and drop into vias, laid around the content and never under a word. Type and outlines are white silkscreen. Copper cyan appears only where the board carries signal: the spine and its vias, LEDs, links, focus, a pulse running along a buried trace, the logo's colons, and the one copper pour. The brand is the original: the live site's hack::peel logo in Space Grotesk, which now sets every word, with JetBrains Mono for times, years, prices and step numbers. The clock chip stays the one signature, wired into the board on wide screens; the sponsors ride a reel of carrier tape; reasons, values and principles each lead with a part icon on a footprint.
keyCharacteristics: One eleven-step neutral ramp at hue 238. Every grey is one of its steps.
Copper cyan is the only accent, and it only ever means signal: trace, via, LED, link, focus, pulse, pour, and the logo's colons.
A soldermask ground with copper routed under it through all the empty board (hero, page heads, under section headings, the margins), tone on tone; no noise, no grid, no glow blob.
The original hack::peel logo, and its face, Space Grotesk, for every word. JetBrains Mono only for times, years, prices and step numbers.
One signature part (the LED clock chip), wired into the board; the rest is a few working parts, footprints and plain type.
A power-up on a single expo ease, then a quiet live board (logo breath, pulses, the tape), all switchable off.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: Every neutral is one of n0 to n10 at hue 238. Nothing else is grey. New surfaces pick a step; they never mix a new grey, a pure black, or a Tailwind gray scale.

rules.name: The Copper Means Signal Rule
rules.body: Cyan is drawn only where a board would carry current or light, plus the logo's colons. Buried copper at rest is neutral (n4); cyan travels along it only as a pulse. Cyan is never a decorative tint, background wash or panel.

rules.name: The Lit LED Rule
rules.body: Light is emitted only by a part that is on: a tier dot, a lit bar segment, the open DIP lamp, the clock matrix dots, a pulse's soft halo, and the logo's colons (the live site's own glow). A glow never spreads far past what emits it.

rules.name: The Mono Is Tabular Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only on times, years, prices and the registration step numbers. It is never used for prose, headings, buttons, labels over headings, or the stat figures.

rules.name: The Standing Part Rule
rules.body: A shadow means a part has height above the board. It is always cast down, with a negative spread so it stays under the part. Flat things (sections, rules, footprints, the stats strip, text) never cast one.

rules.name: The Three Radii Rule
rules.body: There are exactly three corner radii (1px, 2px, 3px), plus 50% for circles and 0 for switch bodies. Never set a larger radius; nothing on a board is pill-shaped or softly rounded.

rules.name: The Brand Face Rule
rules.body: Every word is Space Grotesk, the logo's face. Weight carries hierarchy (400 body, 500 to 600 labels and item heads, 700 heads and figures); heads are sentence case with tight negative tracking. No uppercase labels, no eyebrows.

rules.name: The Copper Under The Mask Rule
rules.body: The ground is a flat colour. The only marks on it are buried copper (the chip's fan-out, each page head's field, the patches and margin trunks), the hatch inside the copper pour, and the footer's edge fingers. Buried copper is tone on tone and unlabelled, fills the empty board rather than sitting in a corner of it, and keeps at least 34px clear of any words or parts (the page-head fields fade out instead).

dos: **Do** use the original logo everywhere the name stands alone (nav, hero, footer, preview card), and set hack::peel as the logo inside heads.
**Do** set every word in Space Grotesk, and keep JetBrains Mono for times, years, prices and step numbers.
**Do** pick every neutral from the n0 to n10 ramp, by its role alias where one exists.
**Do** reach for the existing parts first: a plinth switch, a DIP switch, an LED dot or bar, a footprint, a part icon, buried copper, the tape, the socket.
**Do** fill the empty board with buried copper, tone on tone (n4 traces, n5 vias), 45-degree, unlabelled, keeping 34px clear of words and parts.
**Do** give anything that moves on its own a way to stop: pause on hover and focus, a visible control, and a still version for reduced motion and ATMOSPHERE_ON = false.
**Do** keep to the three radii, plus 50% for circles and 0 for switch bodies.
**Do** start each section on a board rule with a via on the spine.
donts: **Don't** bring back part designators, pad rows under the nav, side pads on switches, mounting holes, test points, pinout leads, a decorative chip in a section's left column, or IC packages around plain content; the client found them weird.
**Don't** run copper under or across text, beside full-width rules (lists, tables), over the copper pour, label it, or light it at rest.
**Don't** bring back the timing-sheet atmosphere: no ambient glow blobs, radial washes, dot field, grid background, or shimmer sweep.
**Don't** add a gradient other than the bar under the hero logo, a second accent hue, or a cyan-tinted panel.
**Don't** glow anything that is not lit (an LED, a pulse, the logo's colons).
**Don't** use pill shapes, radii above 3px, soft rounded cards, or a card kit with drop shadows.
**Don't** use labels as kickers or eyebrows above headings.
**Don't** add looping motion that cannot be stopped, or animate anything when .calm is set.
